text:
A new study uggests that polluted air may reach #brain through the lungs.

Researchers found that 🫁 genetic liability to PM2.5, PM10, NO2 and NOx exposure was causally associated with #asthma, COPD, emphysema, pulmonary fibrosis and lung cancer, with reduced lung function, and with a higher risk of #Alzheimer's disease.

The mechanism they propose: emphysema and COPD lower soluble LRP1, a receptor that clears amyloid-beta from the brain. The #inflammation markers IL-6 and MMP-9 drive this, and lower LRP1 then raises IL-6 and MMP-9 again, which feeds back into #lung damage.

These are genetic inferences from summary-level data, and experimental and clinical work is still needed before the pathways can guide treatment. Even so, the findings add to the case that clean air and good #COPD care could also help protect against dementia.
